title: Hobbies
text: “Is that so, I wonder?”
“……Yeah. Specifically the targets. Theo, you know about it, right?”
“Yes, that’s right. Specifically, there’s a target modeled after a certain person wearing a hat, and it gets moved around as a target during shooting practice.”
“So that’s what Itsuki’s been up to. Well, Itsuki was always mass-producing targets for shooting practice, I say.”
Where he managed to get them from, who knows, but he’d make shooting targets and use them for practice.
“But a hat, is it? What kind of hat, I wonder?”
Specifying a hat like that—Itsuki in this loop really is different.
“He has absolutely no idea.”
“Motoyasu-kun’s always been a bit dense about this sort of thing…”
“You’d think he’d have figured it out by now.”
While saying such things, Father and the others were scolding someone for using a photo of a pig as a target and made them stop, indeed.
“It was a darts-type game. So the nobles of Siltvelt have that sort of thing too.”
“Vof, we do have it, technically.”
“I suppose this counts as a refined pastime too?”
“It is stylish, at least,” Father remarked.
“Motoyasu-kun, you seem like the type to play darts at bars and places like that.”
“Darts, is it? I haven’t done that much of it.”
Less than one might expect, indeed. They had them in arcades and such, but were there really any pigs among the lot who cared that much about darts?
“What about you, Father?”
“I’ve only played a little with friends, nothing serious. Well, Itsuki’s naturally good at it, I’d bet. What about you, Lars-chan?”
“I do it, but really it’s knife-throwing practice.”
Panda, looking bored, skillfully flung a knife she’d been using as tableware and struck the target dead center, I say.
“You did that in the circus too, huh. Well, as long as you’ve got a blade and a target you can play that game, so you see similar things everywhere.”
A case of mixing play with work, indeed.
“Since we’ll be imposing here a bit, Wolf, what’s the major hobby around these parts? Noble hobbies are probably gardening, hunting, horsemanship, that sort of thing?”
“Voff? Certainly, plenty of nobles keep estate gardening as a hobby. Plenty hunt too.”

“Well, I suppose there isn’t that much difference in a nation of demi-humans and beastmen? Ah, but hobbies probably shift depending on whether the species is carnivorous or herbivorous. Apparently there are quite a few unusual plants too.”
This exchange felt like one they’d already had before, I say.
“Horsemanship… time to show off Filolial-sama! Yuki-chan!”
“Yes, ma’am!”

At my request, Yuki-chan showed off an elegant gait in her Filolial form. How about that? Yuki-chan, gleaming in pure white, indeed. Every single step of that gait shone like a model’s walk. How about that? There’s no need to even compare her to some horse, dragon, griffin, or any other so-called mount-class monster, I say.
“Motoyasu-kun’s showing her off to the nobles like ‘behold my prized Yuki-chan’… well, I guess Yuki-chan really does look like a thoroughbred.”
The nobles groaned in admiration at the sight of Yuki-chan.
“She looks fast, but… is she suited for clearing fields?”
“Carrying cargo matters more than anything… but I’ve heard the Filolials raised by the Hero are quite sturdy.”
“Honestly, I’d rather have the one that was walking briskly earlier with that huge beastman on its back. The yellow one.”
Hmm… they seemed to be talking about Elephant and Kou, I sensed.
“Around here it seems draft horses are wanted over racehorses… not quite like heavy-draft racing, but the sturdy, powerful types seem preferred.”
“Vof, there’s no doubt endurance is valued over speed.”
“In our case, the bigger ones would have the aptitude… Luna-chan would fit that, maybe?”
Luna-chan is a girl with a complex about being big-bodied. In terms of build, just as Father and the others say, she’s indeed more of a power type than a speed type.
“Grrrgh! Yuki has both!”
Yuki-chan’s pride seemed sorely wounded, and she cried out. That’s right, indeed! Yuki-chan has plenty of both.
“More importantly, a talking Filolial! Truly a Filolial raised by the Hero-sama.”
“Ooh!” The nobles applauded.
“What are you applauding for! Yuki can do anything! Kou, let’s have a match!”
“Eh? What’s up, Yuki?”
Kou, who’d been eating near Elephant, tilted his head at Yuki-chan as she came at him.
“A match! Let’s race!”
“Kou’s enjoying the party with Elmelo, so later, okay?”
“Now now, Yuki-chan, calm down. Motoyasu-kun, help calm her down too, would you?”
“Understood, indeed. Yuki-chan, it’s fine. You’re a splendid Filolial-sama who serves as everyone’s leader. In a race, you’d surely be number one.”
“Motoyasu-sama! Understood!”
Yuki-chan answered in very good spirits.
“That flip-flop of hers is pretty impressive too. Fitting for someone who prioritizes speed, I suppose.”
“Shh! If you say too much she won’t be able to flip back anymore.”
Incidentally, in the first world, Tiger Girl was just as quick to switch moods when it came to Father.
“So horsemanship counts as a hobby around here too, technically.”
“Vof, it’s convenient for travel, but not that important… we’re fine managing on our own.”
“I suppose that depends on the species too… well, beastmen who really run seriously are pretty fast. Lately Theo’s gotten quick on his feet too.”
“Not as fast as the Filolials though, right?”
“Well, that’s just how it is with us. I see… hunting too—since it affects beastmen’s individual abilities, hunting monsters might practically count as a hobby as well.”
“Voffー. Around here, we’re pretty good at hunting and share the spoils with the people, vof.”
Father nodded along.
“Not exactly the topic to bring up right after arriving, but I’m glad you’re not doing anything like releasing humans and hunting them.”
The moment Father said that, Wolf, Panda, and Elephant all turned their faces away, indeed.
“If I answer honestly… there are stories of tasteless nobles doing that illegally. Vof.”
“That’s a hobby I can’t wrap my head around. I don’t get what anyone gains from doing that.”
“…I hear it’s common in my region.”
“Ah… I see. If I showed Itsuki that, would it cure him of his longing to come here?”
Father’s face turned a little pained.
“Well… honestly, in Shieldfreeden there are apparently stories of the weak being locked up and hunted regardless of race—with firearms, even—and that person crushed it.”
“That’s some deep darkness,” Father muttered under his breath.
“…So it’s already happening. I’d at least want them to target monsters instead.”
“In principle it should be done with wild monsters. Vof.”
“Still, noble hunting is a questionable thing in general. In my world there’s this thing called fox hunting.”
“Vof, that interests me. How’s it different?”
Wolf tilted his head.
“Ah, in Western-style hunting, they apparently release a fox they’ve already caught and then hunt it down. I think using firearms was banned? They release a bunch of hunting dogs instead.”
“Come to think of it, that’s a pretty cruel hobby. Apparently it cost quite a lot of money too,” Father explained.
“Father, Father, in Japan the closest thing would be falconry, I say. Weren’t the expensive hobbies of old Japan fishing, bonsai, and antiques?”
“You really know your stuff in that area, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Indeed. With fishing, once you start getting particular not just about rods but even boats, the spending flows like water, they say. Antiques go without saying.”
Come to think of it… wasn’t there a Sacred Weapon Hero—in that world where Glass lives, the one going off to abandon Rival—who I heard uses a fishing rod? Or was I mistaken?

“Bonsai, huh—that’s a hobby that doesn’t quite match my generation, but in a sense it’s a gardening-type hobby too. Now that I think about it, I feel like I heard bonsai grow huge if you plant them straight in the ground. Was it a university professor who said something like that?”

Father sometimes lets slip things attributed to a “university professor.” Apparently he’d been made to recreate the taste of some late wife’s cooking… I don’t quite understand what relationship this person has built with Father, but there’s a whiff of them being considerate toward Father in various ways, I say.
